subject.title: Feature Request: Agent-triggered context compaction (self-compact tool)

question: Should OpenClaw expose a current-session-only model-callable self-compaction action through session_status, or should model-originated compaction remain unavailable until a different policy boundary exists?
rationale: The implementation shape is bounded, but the core choice is a trust boundary: a model tool call would intentionally abort, compact, and resume active session state without an authorized sender command.

options.title: Approve Narrow Self-Compaction
options.body: Allow a current-session-only session_status action after the linked PR is rebased and security/runtime proof is refreshed.

options.title: Require An Explicit Policy Gate
options.body: Keep the implementation direction but require an operator/tool-policy gate before exposing model-originated compaction.

options.title: Defer To Broader Continuation Design
options.body: Do not land the narrow PR and instead decide self-compaction as part of the larger continuation API discussion.

recommendation.title: Approve Narrow Self-Compaction
recommendation.body: Allow a current-session-only session_status action after the linked PR is rebased and security/runtime proof is refreshed.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature touches `session_status`, active-run behavior, and compaction boundaries where steipete has the clearest introduction and adjacent-history signal.
